english: The highway is faster.
tip: Regular comparatives add -are: snabb becomes snabbare (faster).

english: She paid the bill.
tip: betala takes the bill directly, with no 'for': betalade räkningen = paid the bill.

english: I am in a hurry.
tip: Being in a hurry uses ha, not vara: Jag har bråttom.

english: The country road is more beautiful.
tip: Adjectives ending in -er drop that e before -are: vacker becomes vackrare (more beautiful).

english: I don't agree.
tip: Hålla med (agree) is a two-part verb, and inte goes between the parts: Jag håller inte med.

english: That may be true.
tip: After the modal kan, the next verb is a bare infinitive with no att: Det kan vara sant.

english: That wasn't the intention.
tip: det var inte meningen is a set apology meaning 'I didn't mean to.'

english: They floated on the water.
tip: Flyta is a strong verb, so its past is flöt, not flytade: De flöt på vattnet.

english: We got off the bus.
tip: Kliva av means to get off a vehicle; av is the particle it needs: Vi klev av bussen.

english: We pulled back early.
tip: For vi the reflexive pronoun is oss: dra sig tillbaka becomes Vi drog oss tillbaka (we pulled back).

english: I'm short on time.
tip: Ha ont om means to be short of something: Jag har ont om tid (short on time).

english: It matters every day.
tip: Spela roll means to matter, literally 'play a role': Det spelar roll varje dag.

english: She ate breakfast at seven.
tip: klockan plus a number = at that o'clock: klockan sju = at seven.

english: They thank you for the help.
tip: Tacka pairs with för to mark what you are grateful for: De tackar dig för hjälpen.

english: He gave me his phone number.
tip: sin/sitt/sina all mean 'one's own'; sitt is the ett-word form: gav mig sitt telefonnummer.

target: Jag tänkte att det var du.
english: I thought it was you.
tip: tänka is to think in the sense of reckon or reflect: jag tänkte att det var du.

target: Jag ser det som en möjlighet.
english: I see it as an opportunity.
tip: The frame se something som means 'see as': Jag ser det som en möjlighet.

target: Det går inte att klaga under veckan.
english: You can't complain during the week.
tip: Det går inte att plus a verb means 'you can't' or 'there's no way to': Det går inte att klaga.

target: Barnen vill att vi läser för dem.
english: The children want us to read to them.
tip: Swedish uses vill att plus a clause where English uses an infinitive: vill att vi läser (want us to read).

target: Självklart kommer jag att vara där på festen.
english: Of course I will be there at the party.
tip: Start with an adverb and the verb still comes second, before the subject: Självklart kommer jag.

target: Hur som helst måste vi bestämma oss före fredag.
english: In any case we must decide before Friday.
tip: bestämma sig = make up your mind; use the reflexive: vi måste bestämma oss.

target: Jag längtar efter sommaren, det ska bli så skönt.
english: I long for summer, it will be so nice.
tip: Längta takes efter for the thing you long for: Jag längtar efter sommaren.

target: Han delar med sig av sina kunskaper till alla nya medarbetare.
english: He shares his knowledge with all new coworkers.
tip: 'Sig' is the reflexive for han/hon/de: 'Han tvättar sig' (He washes himself).

english: I tried Swedish meatballs.
tip: Adjectives add -a in the plural: svenska köttbullar = Swedish meatballs.

target: Hon hävdade att det var sant.
english: She maintained that it was true.
tip: "Hävda" (claim/maintain) – a formal reporting verb. Everyday: "sa" (said).

target: Hon grät när hon hörde nyheten.
english: She cried when she heard the news.
tip: gråta is irregular in the past: gråta becomes grät = cried: hon grät.

target: Det var som fan efter jobbet egentligen!
english: That was unbelievable after work actually!
tip: Som fan is a vulgar intensifier, roughly 'as hell'. Use it in casual or vulgar speech only.

target: Vi sjöng sånger runt brasan hela den långa kvällen.
english: We sang songs around the campfire all the long evening.
tip: Sjunga is a strong verb, so its past is sjöng, not sjungde: Vi sjöng sånger.

target: Hon sydde en ny klänning till festen förra helgen.
english: She sewed a new dress for the party last weekend.
tip: Short verbs like sy take -dde in the past: sy becomes sydde = sewed.

target: Barnen frågade oss varför vi inte kunde stanna längre.
english: The children asked us why we could not stay longer.
tip: fråga takes the person as a direct object: frågade oss = asked us.
